newsitem.title: USA: MMI to buy Unionamerica in stock swap.
newsitem.headline: MMI to buy Unionamerica in stock swap.

text.p: MMI Cos Inc. has agreed to acquire Unionamerica Holdings Plc, a London-based insurer, in a stock swap worth about $187.2 million, the companies said Wednesday.

MMI, a healthcare risk management and insurance company based in Deerfield, Ill., said it will begin a tender offer to exchange 0.836 share of its stock for each of Unionamerica's 8.8 million shares outstanding.
MMI shares fell 94 cents to $25.56 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday. Unionamerica's American Depository Receipts rose 87.5 cents to $20.375, also on the NYSE.
The merger is expected to close in the fourth quarter, subject to approval by U.S. and British regulators and the holders of at least 90 percent of Unionamerica's shares.
Unionamerica Chairman Philip Marcell said the need to strengthen share price and carve out a position for the future were the main reasons for the acquisition by MMI Cos Inc.

"As a company of our size quoted on the New York Stock Exchange we found it difficult to have sufficient liquidity in shares to achieve a satisfactory share price, trading off a low potential earnings ratio as we were," Marcell told Reuters.
"We also need to be bigger. Insurance entities are getting bigger and even with a speciality company like us it pays to position yourself for where you want to be tomorrow," he said.

Marcell said there was a great deal of synergy with MMI, whose healthcare policies Unionamerica has reinsured for many years. He said Unionamerica will continue to trade under its own name while operating within the MMI structure.
Unionamerica's operating subsidiary, Unionamerica Insurance Co. Ltd., is a speciality casualty and property reinsurer and insurer operating in the London-based reinsurance and insurance markets.
